terms.comment: In this sense from Seneca and Pliny on: a right granted to one person or body. In Cicero it is a law aimed at one person, mostly against him: in prīvātōs hominēs lēgēs ferrī nōluērunt; id est enim prīvilēgium (Cic. Leg. 3.44, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: an exemption (from taxes or public duties)
terms.comment: The commonest privilege in Roman life: freedom from a burden. Duty-free is immūnis portōriōrum (see duty-free).

phrases.english: certain privileges have been granted to parents

phrases.latin: Druidēs mīlitiae vacātiōnem omniumque rērum habent immūnitātem
phrases.english: the Druids are excused military service and exempt from every other burden

sources: Lewis & Short: privilegium · Lewis & Short: immunitas
